newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore bids to be Asian marine insurance centre.
newsitem.headline: Singapore bids to be Asian marine insurance centre.

text.p: Singapore is bidding to become the focus of Asia's US$1.6 billion regional marine insurance market, the country's insurance commissioner said on Wednesday.

"We are in close dialogue with Lloyd's of London as part of its proposal to establish a greater presence in Singapore and the region," Lim Shu Chiau said in a speech to regional shipowners and insurers.
Lim said her office and the Monetary Authority of Singapore were also in advanced talks with two Protection & Indemnity (P&I) clubs planning operations in the island republic.
The bulk of the world's marine insurance premium is now channelled back to London, particularly to Lloyd's which underwrites about 32 percent of global marine premiums.

Analysts say marine business is worth about US$6.8 billion annually to the London insurance market -- comprising Lloyd's, the Institute of London Underwriters, the London International Insurance and Reinsurance Market Association, and the P&I clubs.
Asian shipowners say they pay about US$1.6 billion a year in insurance premiums.
Sketching out her vision of an Asian marine insurance market, which she said could develop expertise unique to the region, Lim said its creation could have a global impact.
"I think the creation of an Asian marine hull market will be a landmark development and may even change the future course of the international marine insurance market," she told delegates.
Some traditionalists in London view the emerging markets' hopes of establishing a rival marine insurance centre with some scepticism, citing a lack of associated support services.
But Lim said these services already existed.
"In Singapore there are currently several leading hull underwriters providing capacity for a significant number of vessels in Asia.

"In addition, Singapore is also home to reputable and international firms that provide auxiliary marine insurance-related services. Hence a viable marine insurance market already exists here," Lim said.
